channel.title: AI News Digest
channel.description: Official AI product updates from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and GitHub

item.title: GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot
item.description: Learn how GPT-5.6 powers Microsoft 365 Copilot with stronger AI capabilities across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Chat, and Cowork for faster, higher-quality work.

item.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
item.description: More intelligence from every token, stronger performance per dollar, and more capability on demand for your hardest work.

item.title: ChatGPT is now a partner for your most ambitious work
item.description: ChatGPT Work is an agent that can take action across your apps and files, stay with a project for hours if needed, and turn a goal into finished work.

item.title: GPT-5.6 model family
item.description: Released the GPT-5.6 model family, including GPT-5.6 Sol for frontier capability, GPT-5.6 Terra for a balance of intelligence and cost, and GPT-5.6 Luna for efficient, high-volume workloads. The gpt-5.6 alias routes requests to gpt-5.6-sol.

item.title: GPT-5.5 Bio Bug Bounty
item.description: Details about the OpenAI Bio Bounty program

item.title: OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna are now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 family is now rolling out in GitHub Copilot. GPT-5.6 comes in three variants, Sol, Terra, and Luna, so you can match the model to the job, whether that’s reasoning over a large codebase, everyday agentic coding, or fast, cost-efficient assistance.

item.title: Ask Copilot for a repository overview
item.description: You can now ask GitHub Copilot for a high-level overview of any repository you’re exploring for the first time. When you visit the home page of a repository you haven’t contributed to before on github.com, Copilot offers to generate an overview for you.

item.title: UST is bringing Claude to physical AI
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: A new way to reflect on how you use Claude
item.description: Introducing a new way to reflect on and refine how you use Claude. It lets you easily track and visualize how you use Claude, and decide whether that time aligns with your goals.

item.title: Inviting hard questions
item.description: We're asking the public for their hardest questions about AI, and committing to show our work as we address them.

item.title: Ben Bernanke appointed to Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: Separating signal from noise in coding evaluations
item.description: A new analysis from OpenAI reveals issues in SWE-Bench Pro, a popular coding benchmark, raising concerns about reliability and accuracy in evaluating AI models.

item.title: Helping K–12 educators build practical AI skills
item.description: OpenAI Academy and the Walton Family Foundation are bringing hands-on AI Skills Jams to help K–12 educators build practical AI skills for the classroom.

item.title: Introducing GPT-Live
item.description: A new generation of voice models for natural human-AI interaction, now powering ChatGPT Voice.

item.title: Our approach to government and national security partnerships
item.description: Learn how OpenAI approaches government and national security partnerships, with principles for responsible AI use, democratic accountability, and public safety.

item.title: GitHub Mobile: Live notifications for Copilot CLI sessions
item.description: Live coding agent notifications on GitHub Mobile now support remote Copilot CLI sessions, making it easier to stay connected to agent work that starts outside of GitHub Mobile. When a Copilot CLI session is running remotely, GitHub Mobile can surface real-time updates directly on your phone so you can track progress, know when the agent needs your input, and jump back into the session when needed.

item.title: GitHub Mobile: Fix merge conflicts with Copilot cloud agent
item.description: GitHub Mobile now supports fixing pull request merge conflicts with Copilot cloud agent, making it easier to unblock pull requests while you’re on the go. When a pull request has merge conflicts, you can now start the Copilot workflow directly from the pull request merge box on mobile.

item.title: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, June 2026 releases
item.description: This changelog covers VS Code v1.123 through v1.127, shipped throughout June and early July 2026. The latest VS Code releases build on the Copilot experience developers use every day, making it easier to manage agent work, understand usage, choose the right models, and stay in the flow.

item.title: Enterprise-managed OpenTelemetry export for VS Code and CLI
item.description: Organizations can now mandate where GitHub Copilot sends OpenTelemetry (OTel) data, so telemetry flows to an approved collector without each developer setting OTEL_* environment variables. The configuration is delivered through the telemetry block in enterprise-managed settings and applies to both the Copilot Chat extension in VS Code and the agent host process that powers Copilot CLI.

item.title: Deploy managed Copilot settings via MDM in VS Code and CLI
item.description: Enterprise administrators can now deliver managed GitHub Copilot settings directly to devices through native mobile device management (MDM) and file-based configuration, in addition to the existing server-managed channel. This is generally available for GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code.

item.title: Kimi K2.7 now available for Copilot Business and Enterprise
item.description: On July 1, 2026, we announced Kimi K2.7 would be available to Copilot Pro, Pro+, and Max plans. The model is now additionally available on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans.

item.title: Codex as agent provider and agentic enhancements in JetBrains IDEs
item.description: This update brings Codex as a new agent provider in public preview, expands the Customizations editor with Hooks support and richer MCP server management, and introduces custom model support configured by GitHub Copilot Business and Enterprise administrators. It also adds approval settings for Copilot CLI sessions, permission modes selection and debug logs support for the Claude agent, and takes Inline Chat to general availability, alongside a set of performance and reliability improvements.

item.title: Add review cycles and time to adoption phases in the usage API
item.description: The Copilot usage metrics API now reports two additional code-review velocity metrics for each AI adoption phase, extending the adoption phase cohorts fields available in the enterprise and organization reports. Alongside the existing per-phase merge time and merge counts, you can now compare how quickly pull requests are reviewed and how many review cycles they take across your adoption cohorts.

item.title: Never
item.description: You can now set an expiration when you create an API key or an Admin API key in the Claude Console. Choose a preset, a custom duration, or Never. For keys with a lifetime of at least 7 days, Anthropic emails the creator before expiration. Existing keys are unaffected. The Admin API reports each key's expiration in the expires_at field. See Authentication.

item.title: MUFG aims to become AI-native with OpenAI
item.description: MUFG uses ChatGPT Enterprise to build an AI-native organization, improve workflows, and deliver new AI-powered financial services at scale.

item.title: Australian Payments Plus moves faster with ChatGPT and Codex
item.description: See how Australian Payments Plus uses ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to move faster through payments complexity. AP+ saves time, improves quality, and keeps human judgment central.

item.title: Expanding Managed Agents in Gemini API: background tasks, remote MCP and more
item.description: We’re announcing new capabilities in Managed Agents in Gemini API so developers can build reliable, production-ready agents.

item.title: Per-user budgets for cost centers in the billing UI
item.description: Enterprise admins can now create cost center user-level budgets directly in the billing UI where you manage cost centers and budgets. This feature is available for GitHub Enterprise Cloud.

item.title: GitHub Copilot app available to all
item.description: The GitHub Copilot app is now available on every Copilot plan. Sign in with your GitHub account to start agent-driven development from your desktop.

item.title: Copilot Billing Preview app will be retired on August 3
item.description: The Copilot Billing Preview app will be retired on August 3, 2026. If you use it to review your GitHub Copilot spend, you can get even greater visibility directly in your GitHub billing settings.

item.title: GPT-Realtime-2.1, GPT-Realtime-2.1 mini
item.description: Released GPT-Realtime-2.1, an updated realtime reasoning model with improved alphanumeric recognition, silence and noise handling, and interruption behavior. Also released GPT-Realtime-2.1 mini, a faster, lower-cost distilled reasoning model for realtime voice applications.

item.title: Government of Alberta uses Claude to find and fix cybersecurity vulnerabilities
item.description: The Government of Alberta has been using Claude Code with both Opus and Sonnet models to review its systems, find vulnerabilities, and fix them.

item.title: Upcoming deprecation of Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Flash
item.description: We will deprecate Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Flash across all GitHub Copilot experiences (including Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions) on July 31st, 2026: Model Deprecation date Suggested alternative Gemini 2.5 Pro 7-31-2026 Gemini 3.1 Pro Gemini 3 Flash 7-31-2026 Gemini 3.5 Flash Please update your workflows and integrations to use the supported models before these dates.

item.title: Issue fields are now generally available
item.description: Issue fields are now generally available for all GitHub organizations on Free, Team, Enterprise, and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency plans and will ship in GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23. Issue fields bring structured, typed metadata to issues, making it easy to track priority, effort, dates, and custom values consistently across your organization.

item.title: Improved accuracy and coverage in Copilot usage metrics reports
item.description: We’ve made three improvements to the Copilot usage metrics API that make its reports more complete and accurate: GitHub Copilot CLI now reports suggested lines of code, users seen only through server-side telemetry now have their IDE identified, and AI credit consumption is now attributed more completely. What’s new GitHub Copilot CLI now reports suggested lines of code.

item.title: Cost centers now support AI credit pools
item.description: You can now cap how much of your enterprise’s monthly included AI credits a cost center can use. This is available through the REST API today.

item.title: Copilot CLI no longer needs a personal access token in GitHub Actions
item.description: You can now run GitHub Copilot CLI in GitHub Actions using the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN. This means that you no longer need to create and store a personal access token (PAT), eliminating the operational and security risks of managing long-lived PATs for automations at scale.

item.title: Copilot agent session streaming is now in public preview
item.description: GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers with enterprise managed users can now access GitHub Copilot agent session data across all Copilot clients, including: Cloud agents operating on github.com and data resident deployments on ghe.com GitHub Copilot CLI Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Partner IDEs, such as those provided by JetBrains and Eclipse This gives you direct visibility into agent session activity (e.g., prompts, responses, and tool calls) so you can manage AI usage across your enterprise.

item.title: agent-memory-2026-07-22
item.description: The Python (0.116.0), TypeScript (0.110.0), Go (1.56.0), Java (2.48.0), Ruby (1.55.0), PHP (0.36.0), C# (12.35.0), and CLI (1.16.0) SDKs now send agent-memory-2026-07-22 on all memory store calls instead of managed-agents-2026-04-01. If your code passes betas explicitly on memory store calls, replace managed-agents-2026-04-01 with agent-memory-2026-07-22 there rather than adding a second value.

item.title: More details on Fable 5’s cyber safeguards and our jailbreak framework
item.description: What is and isn't blocked by our cyber classifiers, and a first draft of our jailbreak severity framework

item.title: The latest AI news we announced in June 2026
item.description: Here are Google’s latest AI updates from June 2026.

item.title: Set AI credit session limits in Copilot CLI and SDK
item.description: You can now set AI credit session limits in Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot SDK to cap the amount an agent spends in a session. This is especially useful for automation, where no one is actively monitoring the agent’s work.

item.title: New C++ language server config skill for Copilot CLI
item.description: The Microsoft C++ Language Server is now available as a plugin on the Copilot Plugins marketplace. It includes a new built-in setup skill that helps automate project setup, making it easier to generate and maintain the compile_commands.json file the language server needs to understand your code.

item.title: Kimi K2.7 Code is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description: Kimi K2.7 Code, an open-weight model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. This is the first open-weight model offered as a selectable option in the Copilot model picker, giving you more choice and a lower-cost option for your coding workflows.

item.title: GitHub Models is being fully retired on July 30, 2026
item.description: In June, we announced that we are retiring GitHub Models and closed it to new customers. We’re now sharing the timeline for the next step: GitHub Models will be fully retired on July 30, 2026.

item.title: Enterprises can default to auto model selection
item.description: Enterprise administrators can now set model to auto in the enterprise managed-settings.json to make Copilot auto model selection the default for new conversations. Add auto to.github-private/.github/copilot/managed-settings.json in your source organization for enterprise governance so new conversations start with Copilot auto model selection by default.

item.title: Enterprise managed-settings.json is generally available
item.description: GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers can configure AI standards through a managed-settings.json file maintained in a.github-private repository in a selected organization. This allows the enterprise to define new governance and extensibility flows that apply to Copilot clients such as VS Code or Copilot CLI.

item.title: Copilot vision is generally available
item.description: Copilot vision is now generally available. You can attach images and PDFs directly to your chat prompts so Copilot can reason about what it sees alongside your code.

item.title: Copilot CLI auto model selection routes based on task
item.description: Editor’s note (July 1, 2026): Updated the premium request costs to reference AI credits. GitHub Copilot auto model selection now routes to the best model for your task in Copilot CLI, using utilization and model health metrics for a high quality, reliable, and token-efficient experience.

item.title: Browser tools for GitHub Copilot in VS Code are generally available
item.description: Editor’s note (July 1, 2026): Added more detail about which permissions stay under your control and the existing network domain controls. Browser tools for GitHub Copilot in VS Code are now generally available.
